data.narrative:
Elementary Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Arye Barnehama, has raised $66M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in robotics and manufacturing, including peers such as Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis uses Elementary's $66M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $112M. Peer-median analysis examines the 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, yielding a median valuation of $1.6B (range: $1.0B–$2.0B). The peer set skews toward later-stage funding rounds and higher absolute valuations, reflecting sector maturity trends.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $95M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $881M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: the stage-progression method implies significantly lower valuation than peer comps, suggesting either Elementary's unit economics lag peers at comparable stages or the peer set reflects inflation in robotics valuations circa the data collection period. Resolution requires deeper diligence on revenue, growth trajectory, and capital efficiency relative to the named comparables.
